name: mira-test
construction: The test set has English questions, Urdu translations of those questions, and unanswerable questions in both languages. Gold pages are 1-based pages of the ingested PDF. Every answerable item stores a short quotation that occurs on a cited page. Urdu questions and Urdu reference answers were written as translations of the English items; they are not an independently collected Urdu information-need study, and there was no second annotator. Nine documents are research papers. Three state CC BY 4.0 inside the PDF (arXiv 2103.14460v1, 2103.14455v1, and 2106.16239v9). Six are ACL Anthology papers from 2019-2024. The Anthology states that materials published in or after 2016 are under CC BY 4.0 (https://aclanthology.org/). One additional document is the Urdu Wikipedia article مصنوعی ذہانت, revision 11740367, under CC BY-SA 4.0. Questions tagged corpus=urdu_doc are about that article, including English questions over Urdu text. The pilot file is disjoint and is used only to set evidence-gate thresholds. It is not scored in the reported tables. This is a project benchmark, not a community dataset.
